title: Telemetry evolution — annotated sprint notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick annotated sprint notes for telemetry evolution work — goal is a compact, actionable list of metric/tracing changes, dashboard tagging, and a lightweight rollout plan that we can iterate on during the sprint. This is intentionally informal: notes from pairing sessions, follow-ups, TODOs, and sample queries.

Context recap (one-liner):
We need to reduce alert noise, improve investigation speed for token-serving regressions, and make dashboards cheaper to query for low-touch SRE operations while preserving enough fidelity for model rollouts.

Top problems observed (summary):
- Alert volume spikes during multi-tenant bursts; paging is noisy and many pages are for transient cold-cache events.
- High-cardinality tag explosion from tenant metadata and prompt-label tags — query CPU & storage costs.
- Traces are undersampled for low-severity latency regressions; sampling prioritizes errors only.
- Dashboards across teams use inconsistent tag vocabularies (env, deployment, model_variant, route) — makes cross-team triage slow.

Goals for this sprint (measurable):
1) Reduce alert pages for transient cold-cache by 60% by adding a short-circuit suppression window and session-warmth gating.
2) Implement tiered trace sampling that increases trace capture rate for 95th+ latency when error=false by end of sprint.
3) Publish dashboard tagging taxonomy and update top-3 ops dashboards to conform.
4) Prototype a compact aggregate metric (session_warmth_index) and add to operator heatmap widget.

Metric definitions (proposed canonical set, minimal):
- request.count: total inference requests received (label: route, model, env, tenant) — integer counter, 1s scrape
- request.latency_ms.p50/p90/p95/p99: end-to-end latency excluding client TLS time (label: route, model_variant) — histogram summary
- token.emit.count: tokens emitted by runtime (label: model_variant, quantization_profile) — counter aggregated per-minute
- kv_cache.hit_ratio: fraction of requests that benefited from prefix/KV cache (0..1) (label: tenant, deployment_region) — gauge derived from hits/attempts
- session_warmth_index: compact 0..1 score estimating cache/context warmness for a session (labels: tenant, route) — derived metric, see formula below
- fallback.rate: % of requests that use fallback model/region (label: fallback_reason) — rolling-% over 5m

session_warmth_index — candidate formula (we will iterate):
- s = clamp( (recent_kv_hits / max(1, recent_requests)) * 0.6 + (historical_user_cache_affinity * 0.4), 0, 1)
- recent_* are 5-minute rolling windows. We want a cheap, single-digit-cardinality index (bucket tenants into heat bands).

Metric labels and cardinality rules (practical constraints):
- Allowed high-cardinality labels: model_variant (if we have < 80 variants globally), deployment_region (small), env (prod/stage)
- Forbidden per-request labels: full tenant_id, raw_prompt_hash, user_handle — replace with tenant cohort or hashed buckets when necessary.
- Tenant-level slicing should be via tenant_cohort (Low/Medium/High || reserved/dedicated) to avoid high-cardinality explosion.

Tracing plan (sampling + instrumentation notes):
- Baseline: always capture one trace per request for 1% of requests (global reservoir), boosted to 10% for requests that hit p95+ latency or trigger a fallback.
- Severity-weighted reservoir: keep more traces when latency is high but error=false to catch slow token-paths.
- Session-affinity sampling: if a session has already generated an interesting trace (p95+), increase trace sampling for the next 30s for that session_id (use session_cohort id).
- For multi-model fanout flows capture lightweight child spans with minimal metadata (span name, duration_ms, model_variant, tenant_cohort) and only capture full input/prompt for sampled errors or flagged test routes.
- Trace redaction: prompts and PII must be stripped at the agent before trace export. Add a compute-safe hashing step for prompt fingerprints.

Dashboard tagging taxonomy (one page cheat-sheet):
- base tags: env, deployment_region, service, route
- model tags: model_family, model_variant, quant_profile
- op tags: tenant_cohort, session_band (warm/cold/warm-ish), rollout_phase (canary/baseline/force)
- alert tags: alert_owner, severity, mitigation_playbook_id

Dashboard migration checklist (apply to top-3 ops dashboards first):
- [ ] Replace tenant_id slices with tenant_cohort where used in panels
- [ ] Add session_warmth_index panel and use it as a drilldown filter
- [ ] Add cost cap annotation + query budget tag for each panel (est. monthly query cost)
- [ ] Ensure all panels accept a standardized time-range param (t0, t1 override) and show query latency in a mini-cell
- [ ] Add link to runbook and trace sample query for investigation (see linked_artifacts)

Sample investigation query snippets (prometheus-like pseudo-SQL):
- p95 latency by route (5m window):
  quantile_over_time(0.95, request_latency_ms_bucket{job=\"inference\"}[5m]) by (route)
- cold-cache surge detection (per-ten-cohort):
  increase(request.count{session_band=\"cold\"}[10m]) / increase(request.count[10m]) > 0.2
- trace-backed slow-paths (post-replay join suggestion):
  SELECT span_name, avg(duration_ms), count(*) FROM traces WHERE timestamp > now-1h AND duration_ms > 200 GROUP BY span_name ORDER BY avg(duration_ms) DESC LIMIT 20;

Sampling knobs we want exposed in Console (config surface):
- global_reservoir_pct (float) — default 1.0
- latency_boost_threshold_ms (int) — default 200ms
- post_trigger_window_s (int) — default 30s for session affinity
- per-tenant_max_traces_per_min (int) — default 5 for high cohort

Cost and query budget notes (short):
- Target: keep top-3 dashboards < 300 queries/day total for oncall usage. If above, migrate heavy panels to precomputed rollups or downsampled traces.
- Precompute weekly rollups for token.emit.count by model_family to avoid repeated heavy aggregation.

Open questions / discussion items (to resolve in next sync):
1) session_warmth_index weighting: how much should historical affinity matter vs immediate KV hits? (Ruth to propose weighting experiments)
2) Tenant cohort mapping lifecycle: who owns mapping? product or SRE? (action: Priya to draft policy)
3) Storage retention tiers for traces (hot 7d, warm 30d, archived 1y?) — cost tradeoffs and compliance implications (Leo + infra)
4) How to instrument fallback.rate consistently for cross-region fallbacks where request is proxied (Miguel assigned to prototype)

Sprint action items (who, what, eta):
- Asha: wireframe session_warmth_index derivation and example dashboard widget (eta: 2026-01-12)
- Miguel: implement trace-sampling config toggle and session-affinity stub in staging (eta: 2025-12-22)
- Ruth: run experiments to validate cold-cache suppression window and propose threshold for suppression (eta: 2026-01-05)
- Leo: estimate trace storage cost for proposed retention tiers and produce cost per tenant_cohort (eta: 2025-12-29)
- Priya: write tenant_cohort ownership policy draft and add to linked_artifacts (eta: 2025-12-18)

Meeting notes / sync cadence:
- Weekly 30m sync on Tuesdays 10:30am PT (telemetry squad) — quick status, blockers, demo small dashboards.
- Ad-hoc pairing on sampling experiments; use #obs-sampling Slack thread and attach logs to OBS-1243.

Quick reference: useful links and runbook snippets
- Runbook for cold-cache alert: confluence:runbook-cold-cache-v1
- Trace-sampling config reference: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-config/tree/main/sampling
- Investigation query library (living doc): confluence:obs-investigation-library

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep initial changes conservative: small sampling boosts, avoid full tenant-level sampling changes until we measure cost.
- When in doubt, add a cohort instead of a raw label.
- Prefer derived, compact metrics over retaining raw high-cardinality labels.

End of sprint notes — will update after first round of experiments and show a before/after alert volume graph.
